summary: Iteration 13 retest of the two iter-12 bugs plus smoke checks. RESULT: BOTH BUGS FIXED. (1) Font-size persistence: PUT /api/settings now returns 200 (was 422). Decreased 18→16 via mode-font-size-decrease-btn, reloaded, value stayed at 16. (2) Per-bubble delete on assistant: ran Collaborate with a passage that produced an em-dash-heavy reply (multiple '—' chars: 'dust — that particular smell', '— half-thought —', '— Later —'). Clicking mode-turn-assistant-1-delete + accepting the confirm dialog COMPLETELY removes the assistant bubble (no residual fragment, no mid-word truncation). Additional smoke checks all PASS: (3) Follow-up delete — after sending mode-followup-input + mode-followup-btn, deleting mode-turn-user-2 removes both the follow-up user AND its assistant reply while preserving user-0 + assistant-1 text integrity (no mid-word truncation — assistant-1 first-80 chars unchanged, full content preserved). (4) User-0 delete edge case — clicking mode-turn-user-0-delete clears mode-passage-view AND the assistant reply remains rendered (re-indexed to mode-turn-assistant-0). (5) Session rename via double-click on history-item-<id> opens history-rename-input-<id>, Enter saves, row displays new label 'RETEST13 Rename OK'.

issues: One PUT /api/settings fires with 401 before auth cookie is validated on first mount (harmless race — the .catch() swallows it and the next PUT after auth resolves at 200 — but slightly noisy in Network log).

critical_code_review_comments: Follow-up delete behaviour: when mode-turn-user-2 is deleted, mode-turn-assistant-3 is also swallowed and its content is appended into mode-turn-assistant-1 (length 840 -> 1701). Text integrity is preserved (first-80 chars unchanged, no truncation), and this matches the review's 're-indexes cleanly' allowance, but the visual result is that the follow-up assistant reply merges into the initial reply rather than remaining as a separate bubble. If product intent is 'delete only the clicked bubble', the delete handler should also drop the orphaned assistant that followed. Consider making this explicit.

settings.jsx still swallows PUT failures with .catch(() => {}). The 422 was invisible for iterations because of this. Recommend surfacing errors (toast or console.error) even now that the backend is fixed, to catch future regressions early.
TopBar font-size PUT fires once on initial mount before auth cookie is confirmed → 401. Not user-visible but pollutes Network tab. Gate the debounced PUT on !!user or on the initial GET completing.

success_rate.backend: not tested (frontend-only iteration; observed PUT /api/settings 200 during UI exercise, 401 only on pre-auth mount)

seed_data_creation: Created two new Collaborate history sessions during retest: 'The Locked Box In The Attic' (em-dash reply test) and 'Rain Ropes and Fogged Glass' (follow-up + user-0 delete tests). Renamed one existing history session to 'RETEST13 Rename OK'. Safe to leave or clean via db.ai_history.delete_many({user_id: <testwriter uid>, title: {$in: ['The Locked Box In The Attic','Rain Ropes and Fogged Glass','RETEST13 Rename OK']}}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration-12 blockers are fully resolved. Sentinel change (\u0001BEGIN_U\u0001 / \u0001BEGIN_A\u0001) in ModeWorkspace.jsx parseTranscript correctly avoids em-dash collisions — verified with a reply containing 5+ em-dash occurrences. Settings PUT returns 200 after backend Settings.user_id was made Optional[str]=None. Only observations left are minor: (a) one pre-auth 401 on settings PUT at mount, (b) deleting a follow-up user turn also merges the subsequent assistant reply into the prior bubble — product decision required whether this is desired UX.
rca of the issue: N/A — both iter-12 bugs verified fixed. Fix 1: backend/server.py:163 Settings.user_id changed to Optional[str]=None; PUT endpoint still overrides with auth uid before persistence — validated by observing 200 responses in Network log. Fix 2: ModeWorkspace.jsx parseTranscript now uses control-character sentinels \u0001BEGIN_U\u0001 / \u0001BEGIN_A\u0001 (with legacy em-dash fallback for old sessions). Verified by producing an LLM reply containing multiple em-dashes and confirming a single assistant bubble parses as a single turn, deletable in one click.
